title: Small matched grant-graph population experiment

contracts.independent_issue: Separately issued grants are distinct even when subject/agent labels match.
contracts.credential_copy: A lossless copy of one credential remains one grant, with the same ID and revocation outcome.
contracts.leaf_local_revocation: Revoking a leaf denies that grant and its copies without denying unrelated grants.
contracts.display_rename: Model-level presentation alias only; credential and signed subject are untouched. SDK-native rename is NOT tested.
contracts.depth: Existing independently executed APC and MandateKit depth results are referenced, not newly mutation-tested here.

probe_definitions.target_verdict: All pre-revocation legal grants allow; after revoke only the selected target's DENY is asserted.
probe_definitions.target_condition: The same target probe plus a revocation-specific denial category.
probe_definitions.population_contract: Additional inputs/assertions: unique independent IDs, every unrelated grant still allows, and copied credential identity/outcome. This probe inspects more cases; no equal-cost superiority claim.

label_semantics.apc: The exposed string is Principal.principal_id, a signed identity identifier, not a separate display label. Repetition means multiple issuance calls for the same principal; distinct strings mean distinct principals.
label_semantics.mandatekit: The issuance-time string is subject.agent_id; the independently generated grant ID is mandate_id.
label_semantics.behalf: The issuance-time string is the agent caveat; the grant is identified by its terminal chain ID.
label_semantics.alpha_renamed_same_label: A separately issued graph uses a consistently substituted subject string. This is not an SDK rename of an existing credential.
label_semantics.cross_framework_match: Graph topology and requested grant contracts are matched. The three APIs' identity/display-label models are not asserted equivalent.

within_condition_prior_run.kind: reference to prior executed saved audit, NOT rerun by this campaign

prior_art.relationship: Lifecycle, identity, reason-specific conformance, paired vectors and mutation testing are prior art. This artifact adds only the explicit matched API population measurements and source-specific APC attribution.

limits: Five small convenience-selected graph shapes, three label settings; these are not independent samples of deployments.
Same-shape label transformations are correlated tests, not extra empirical prevalence evidence.
Three hand-selected Behalf faults only; no representative mutation coverage or upstream-suite mutation score is claimed.
Faults are artificial changes to issuance ID generation or a pluggable revocation store; they are not new Behalf vulnerabilities.
No test-suite comparison: these are explicitly defined probe layers, not measurements of published SDK tests.
The population probe sees more inputs than the target-only probes, so the sensitivity difference is expected coverage, not a new testing principle.
Display alias renaming is out-of-band model metadata. Signed agent names are not edited; no native rename API was tested.
APC principal_id and the other SDKs' subject/agent strings have different identity semantics; issuance-label variants are not a claim of physical identity equivalence.
Native Behalf and MandateKit success is limited to these configured in-process grants and verification decisions, not an overall security ranking.
Grant IDs, not physical AI-agent identities, are measured; stolen/copied credentials are not assumed to identify separate workers.
No descendants-cascade contract is imposed on APC. Only leaf-local selectivity is tested.
No live agent, service, transaction, network action or production exploit is involved.
